deck_name: 君の名は。 Ch.8 君の名は。 — Grammar & Expressions
source: 新海誠『君の名は。』(角川つばさ文庫), 第八章「君の名は。」
notes: The final chapter moves between 瀧's job hunt, years of unexplained longing for both 瀧 and 三葉, and their meeting after a glimpse between two trains. This deck covers the N2/N1 patterns and literary devices that carry that mood: concession and trends for the job hunt, can't-help-it feelings and 'without ever' for the longing, and rhetorical suspicion and 'as if' for the meeting. The list is built from the chapter's scenes and the novel's style, not transcribed page by page, so a few patterns may sit a chapter early or late. Words and patterns already taught in an earlier chapter's deck aren't repeated here, even when this chapter uses them again.

priority_guide.high: Learn before or while reading this chapter — it carries the scene.
priority_guide.medium: Useful; context usually helps if you forget it.
priority_guide.low: Recognition is enough — look it up once, don't over-drill.

difficulty_guide.two_above: N1 / literary — ambitious; learn to recognise it.

kanji_difficulty_guide.easy: Kanji are common; readable at N3.
kanji_difficulty_guide.medium: One or more kanji may trip you — drill the reading.
kanji_difficulty_guide.hard: Rare kanji or irregular reading — learn the kana form first.

cards.pattern: N + を通じて / を通して
cards.scene: In interviews, 瀧 tries to put into words what he hopes to achieve through architecture.
cards.context: Form: N + を通じて (more formal) / を通して. Two uses: (1) means or medium — 仕事を通じて社会に貢献する; (2) throughout a span — 一年を通じて (all year round). を通して leans toward a deliberate channel ('via someone'); を通じて is the polished choice in interviews and speeches.
cards.example_sentence: 建築の仕事を通じて、人々の暮らしを支えたいと考えています。
cards.example_reading: けんちく の しごと を つうじて、 ひとびと の くらし を ささえたい と かんがえて います。
cards.example_meaning: I hope to support people's lives through work in architecture.

cards.pattern: Vて / Adjくて / Naで + ならない
cards.scene: Both 瀧 and 三葉 can't shake the feeling that they've lost or forgotten something.
cards.context: Form: Vて (feeling/perception verbs, esp. 気がする) / Adj-くて / Na-で + ならない: 気がしてならない, 心配でならない, 悔しくてならない. A feeling too strong to suppress — more literary than 〜てしょうがない / 〜てたまらない. Where 〜ような気がする (N3) is a mild 'I feel as if', 〜気がしてならない is that feeling refusing to go away.
cards.example_sentence: 誰かとの約束を忘れている気がしてならない。
cards.example_reading: だれか と の やくそく を わすれて いる き が して ならない。
cards.example_meaning: I can't shake the feeling that I've forgotten a promise I made to someone.

cards.pattern: plain form + わけでもない
cards.scene: Neither of them is waiting for anyone in particular — and yet they keep scanning crowds.
cards.context: Form: plain form (Na-adj 〜な, N 〜という) + わけでもない. Rules out an obvious explanation: 悲しいわけでもないのに涙が出る (it's not that I'm sad, yet tears come). The も adds 'nor is it…', often after other reasons have been rejected. Compare わけではない (plain denial) and わけがない (impossible).
cards.example_sentence: 誰かを待っているわけでもないのに、つい駅の人混みを見てしまう。
cards.example_reading: だれか を まって いる わけ でも ない のに、 つい えき の ひとごみ を みて しまう。
cards.example_meaning: It's not as if I'm waiting for anyone, yet I find myself watching the station crowds.

cards.pattern: Vdictionary + ともなく (+ same verb)
cards.scene: On trains and in quiet moments, they gaze out at the city without really seeing it.
cards.context: Form: V-dictionary + ともなく, usually followed by the same or a similar verb: 見るともなく見る (look without really looking), 聞くともなく聞く. Describes idle, half-conscious action. With question words: どこからともなく (from somewhere or other), 誰からともなく (without anyone in particular starting). Literary.
cards.example_sentence: 見るともなく車窓の景色を眺めていた。
cards.example_reading: みる とも なく しゃそう の けしき を ながめて いた。
cards.example_meaning: I was idly watching the scenery outside the train window, not really looking at it.

cards.scene: Years pass with the ache still unexplained and the person still not found.
cards.context: Form: Vない + まま (〜ないままだ / 〜ないまま〜する). まま means a state continues unchanged; with ない it stresses that something never happened while time moved on: 理由がわからないまま (still not knowing why). Often paired with ずっと: ずっと〜ないままでいる.
cards.example_sentence: 言いたいことを言えないまま、卒業の日が来てしまった。
cards.example_reading: いいたい こと を いえない まま、 そつぎょう の ひ が きて しまった。
cards.example_meaning: Graduation day came without my ever saying what I wanted to say.

cards.pattern: Vて + 以来 / N + 以来
cards.scene: Years have gone by since the events of the earlier chapters, and the strange feeling has stayed ever since.
cards.context: Form: Vて + 以来, or N + 以来 (あの日以来, 卒業以来). A state that began at a point in the past and still continues. Unlike 〜てから (simple sequence), 以来 stresses the unbroken stretch up to now, and has a written feel.
cards.example_sentence: 東京に来て以来、一度も故郷に帰っていない。
cards.example_reading: とうきょう に きて いらい、 いちど も こきょう に かえって いない。
cards.example_meaning: Ever since coming to Tokyo, I haven't been back to my hometown even once.

cards.pattern: A ような、B ような + N
cards.simpler_synonym: 〜ような気もするし、〜ような気もする
cards.scene: Their feelings in this chapter rarely have one name — sad and nostalgic, hopeful and afraid at once.
cards.context: Form: A (plain form / i-adj) + ような、B + ような + noun (気持ち, 気分, 感じ). Lists two, often opposite, impressions to describe a feeling that won't settle into one word: 嬉しいような悲しいような気持ち. A favourite device of emotional narration.
cards.example_sentence: 卒業の日は、嬉しいような寂しいような、不思議な気分だった。
cards.example_reading: そつぎょう の ひ は、 うれしい ような さびしい ような、 ふしぎ な きぶん だった。
cards.example_meaning: Graduation day felt strange — somehow both happy and lonely.

cards.pattern: N / な-adj + ではあるまいか; V / い-adj + のではあるまいか
cards.scene: As they search the streets, each half-wonders whether the feeling is real or only imagined.
cards.context: Form: N / な-adj + ではあるまいか; verb / い-adj + のではあるまいか. まい is the literary negative of conjecture/volition (≈ ないだろう), so あるまいか ≈ ないだろうか — a bookish 〜のではないだろうか. まい also appears in 〜ようか〜まいか ('whether to ~ or not'): 行こうか行くまいか迷う.
cards.example_sentence: この気持ちは、ただの思い込みではあるまいか。
cards.example_reading: この きもち は、 ただ の おもいこみ では ある まい か。
cards.example_meaning: Might this feeling not be just my imagination?

cards.scene: Like テッシー and サヤちん sitting near 瀧 in a café without his noticing, many near-meetings in this chapter come to nothing.
cards.context: Form: Vない-stem + ずじまい (だ / で終わる); する → せずじまい. The chance passed and the thing never happened, with a note of regret: 聞かずじまい, 言えずじまい, 会えずじまい. Compare 〜ないまま (neutral 'still not').
cards.example_sentence: 引っ越しの前に、隣のおばあさんにお礼を言えずじまいだった。
cards.example_reading: ひっこし の まえ に、 となり の おばあさん に おれい を いえず じまい だった。
cards.example_meaning: I never got to thank the old lady next door before I moved.

meanings: What is N? / What about N? (predicate left unsaid)
cards.scene: The chapter's title echoes the question the two ask each other at the very end.
cards.context: Form: N + は (+ rising tone or ？), predicate dropped: お名前は？ = What's your name? The title 君の名は。 does the same with literary 名 (な) and a full stop instead of a question mark, so it reads as an unfinished question — or an unfinished statement ('Your name is…'). Leaving the predicate unsaid is common in titles and emotional speech.
cards.example_sentence: 「で、その人の名前は？」と友達に聞かれて、答えられなかった。
cards.example_reading: 「で、 その ひと の なまえ は？」 と ともだち に きかれて、 こたえられなかった。
cards.example_meaning: "So, what's the person's name?" my friend asked, and I couldn't answer.
